items.desc:
Große Sprachmodelle (Large Language Models, LLMs) haben bemerkenswerte Fähigkeiten in einer Vielzahl von Aufgaben gezeigt. Ihre Leistung nimmt jedoch häufig in hochspezialisierten Domänen ab, die präzises strukturelles Schlussfolgern, Konsistenz und domänenspezifisches Wissen erfordern. Im Bereich des elektronischen Hardware-Designs haben bestehende LLMs Schwierigkeiten mit der strukturellen und semantischen Komplexität von Schaltungsbeschreibungen. Hardware-Designs werden als miteinander verbundene Graphen dargestellt, einschließlich Netzlisten, Schaltplänen und hierarchischen […] . Diese Darstellungen enthalten wesentliche Informationen, die bei der Umwandlung in rein sequenziellen Text verloren gehen.
 Als Teil unseres Teams werden Sie neuartige Methoden erforschen, um generative KI-Systeme an spezialisierte Domänen anzupassen, indem Sie strukturiertes symbolisches Wissen integrieren – ohne auf umfangreiches erneutes Training der Modelle angewiesen zu sein.
 Ihre Untersuchung wird sich auf Mechanismen konzentrieren, die es Large Language Models (LLMs) und anderen Foundation Models ermöglichen, externe Wissensrepräsentationen wie Wissensgraphen, Ontologien und formale Designrepräsentationen zu nutzen, während die Schlussfolgerungsfähigkeiten symbolischer Systeme erhalten bleiben.
 Sie werden innovative Ansätze entwickeln, die es generativen KI-Modellen ermöglichen, direkt mit diesen strukturierten Repräsentationen zu interagieren, um präziseres Schlussfolgern, Designunterstützung, Verifikation und Codegenerierung zu ermöglichen.

items.title: PhD - Neurosymbolic Reasoning for Domain-Adaptive Generative AI
items.desc:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across a wide range of tasks. However, their performance often degrades in highly specialized domains that require precise structural reasoning, consistency, and domain-specific knowledge. In electronic hardware design, existing LLMs struggle with the structural and semantic complexity of circuit descriptions. Hardware designs are represented as interconnected graphs, including netlists, schematics, and hierarchical design projects. These representations carry essential information that is lost when converted into purely […] quential text.
 As a part of our team, you will research novel methods for adapting generative AI systems to specialized domains by integrating structured symbolic knowledge, without relying on extensive model retraining.
 Your investigation will focus on mechanisms that enable Large Language Models (LLMs) and other foundation models to leverage external knowledge representations such as knowledge graphs, ontologies, and formal design representations while preserving the reasoning capabilities of symbolic systems.
 You will develop innovative approaches that enable generative AI models to interact directly with these structured representations, allowing for more precise reasoning, design assistance, verification, and code generation.
 Through your work, you will make a key contribution to the development of next-generation AI systems that combine the flexibility of neural models with the reliability, interpretability, and structured reasoning capabilities of symbolic representations.

items.desc:
How to avoid learning too much - safe and efficient learning for control 
 Job description 
Inefficient operation of industrial systems, electricity production, and heating systems in buildings is currently responsible for over 50% of overall greenhouse gases emissions. Improving energy efficiency of energy-intensive sectors by implementing advanced control systems has the potential to both improve efficiency and reduce the costs, all while continuing to meet safety requirements. The flexibility of safe and adaptive learning control methods makes them crucial for safety-critical applications. […] requirements. The flexibility of safe and adaptive learning control methods makes them crucial for safety-critical applications. A key difficulty in these learning-based approaches lies in the fact that the algorithm must simultaneously learn the model and guarantee safety. This dual requirement significantly impacts the computational cost of the learning algorithm, particularly in situations where the optimal decision evolves over time. We now aim to develop computationally efficient safe learning methods for time-varying optimal control problems.
Existing safe learning algorithms usually assume that they have unlimited access to the experiments and thus unlimited new data. Approaches using limited data sets have been restricted to Bayesian optimization without safety constraints. Moreover, the algorithms typically rely on the repetitive nature of the experiments, for instance in robotics or precision manufacturing. The unlimited data combined with repetitiveness limit the applicability of safe learning algorithms in problems evolving over time, such as residential buildings. This PhD project will explore the connection between the dynamics of the optimized system with numerical properties of optimization algorithms to provide a framework for safe learning with minimal interactions over time. items.title: PhD in Bioreactor-based preservation of human heart valves
items.desc:
Are you fascinated by the potential of maintaining heart valves outside of the human body?
 Are you eager to contribute to better and sustainable healthcare at the interface of engineering and biology?
 Are you passionate about inspiring and mentoring students and working in a high-end collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment?
 Are you our next PhD candidate in bioreactor-based preservation of human heart valves?
 Information 
The Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) is seeking a highly talented, ambitious and passionate PhD candidate to investigate and further develop […]  model of heart valve preservation. We aim to develop a way to keep heart valves alive outside of the human body using dynamic bioreactors where the valves open and close as they do in the human body. As the successful candidate, your research with us will contribute to broader efforts to culture living cardiac tissues and to study their function and their response to immune cells and immune protective technology, closely aligned with our BIOSHIELD consortium funded by the Dutch Heart Foundation. Our group’s research concentrates on developing and improving heart valve replacements in young children born with congenital heart disease. The current valve replacement options available in clinical practice cannot adapt to the growing heart of a child and can elicit immune responses that destroy and calcify implanted valves. Therefore, these young patients require multiple invasive operations throughout their lives. We investigate how to develop a living valve that can grow with the heart and is safe from immune rejection. Alongside our advances in in-situ tissue engineering of heart valves, we investigate strategies for immune shielding and culture of living human donor heart valves as an alternative approach.
